description: A heavy-stock poster, its edges scorched like it was printed too close to something on fire. The whole frame is motion: every figure in it smeared and half-blurred, mid-dive, mid-shout, grit and burning paper hanging in the air. Every figure except Kiyo, who's rendered in hard perfect focus, kneeling, and entirely still. A lab coat pulled on over borrowed plate, its pockets sagging with reagent vials and a folded page of his own working. One lens of his glasses cracked straight across. Laid out on the ground in front of him with the reverence of an operating theatre: calipers, a decanting rig, a row of glass ampoules racked in foam, a notebook open on a column of figures, and the opened guts of something not yet finished. And every weapon in the picture is his. The blurred figures fighting around him are carrying nothing but his work: a rifle grown out of a junction box and a length of scaffold pipe, a launcher that began life as a fire extinguisher, a wicked little pistol with the maker's mark scratched into the slide by hand. He's passing another one up over his shoulder into a hand that has come down for it, and he isn't watching where it goes. He isn't ducking. He isn't looking up. Whatever is coming apart two metres behind him has plainly been assessed, weighed, and filed as somebody else's job. His job is on the ground in front of him, and it's nearly done. KIYO DIDN'T LOOK UP. Stencilled below in service-manual type: "give him ten minutes and a junction box and he'll hand you a weapon, a bomb, or a way out, his call, and he has never yet chosen wrong." Across the top of the frame, entering from the torn left edge, hangs the underside of a wing that nothing in this picture explains. A real strand of copper wire is threaded through two punched holes, worried bright by passing thumbs.
name: hero poster: KIYO, THE MAN WHO DIDN'T LOOK UP
